physicalNotes: Radius 6.558 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: radius 5.695 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 94.567 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.602) and temperature; scaled from the paper's distance, 117.096 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 5.695 x 134.84/117.096 = 6.558 solar radii (luminosity 125.4); scaled from the paper's distance, 117.096 pc, to the cluster's, 134.84 pc: at a fixed temperature the radius grows with the distance, so 5.695 x 134.84/117.096 = 6.558 solar radii (luminosity 125.4) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 4,562,401 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7548 +/- 2496 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: effective temperature 7548 +/- 2496 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.495) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
